newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures came under pressure on Wednesday with other major bond markets from selling by U.S. funds and after a brief bounce on GLOBEX extended their losses further, traders said.
Some traders said there was a good chance the June contract would test support at 129.32, the top of a gap on charts down to 129.16. The contract was testing support at 129.46 on GLOBEX.

Traders and analysts said the subdued market response to the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged, combined with U.S. data suggesting first quarter growth could be revised higher, had soured sentiment in bond markets.

Traders said one U.S. house had sold more than 20,000 lots in each of the French, German and U.K. bond markets during the past two days for a U.S. fund, while others, following technical levels on charts, had amplified the selloff.

"I think the move was triggered by the poorer tone in the U.S...the fear is the Fed merely postponed a rate rise to July," Andrew Davies at London Bond Broking said. "On top of that the (U.S. March) trade deficit came in at only 8.5 billion. In that case first quarter GDP could be revised up."
U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said first quarter growth looked more like six percent than 5.6 percent.

One trader said in the current nervous environment he would not rule out a decline in the French bond future to 128.94. Another said the technical picture in the French and German markets had taken a marked turn for the worse.
Traders said the French cash market was very quiet on Wednesday. The 10-year spread between French and German bond yields was stable at minus 15 basis points during the decline.
PIBOR and the French franc were relatively stable. June PIBOR settled up two basis points at 96.51 while the franc was at 3.3682 against the mark compared with 3.3679 late on Tuesday.
With a blackout on opinion poll results ahead of the first round of a French parliamentary election on May 25 there was little domestic news for French financial markets to get their teeth into.
Analysts said most were still banking on a return to power for the centre-right coalition albeit with significantly reduced majority.
